claims.text: The deviation is established on the governing trace figure. POL-RD-01 measures the excess on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 17.57 km here, and expressly forbids citing the rounded convenience copy on the trip record (17.60 km). Against the platform optimal of 14.0 km the excess is 3.57 km — 25.5% of optimal, above the 20% establishment threshold, and 3.57 km absolute, above the 0.8 km threshold. Both tests pass, and the derived block on the trace records the status as 'established'.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same identifier TRP-00107 and consistent times (trace first fix 21:13:42 against started_at 21:13:40), and the trace shows an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause; his bare assertion that 'the CTE into town is always jammed' cites no traffic_advisory ID and, under POL-RD-08, is a general assertion that carries no weight and is discarded.

Even measured on the stricter footing POL-RD-08 applies to a below-30% excess, the claim is corroborated beyond the gps_trace from the POL-RD-07(ii) list: the driver's own counterparty_statement admits the route — 'I went by Newton and Kim Seng' — which is an admission of the off-optimal corridor, and the chat log shows the rider observing the exit at Whitely while the driver did not dispute leaving the CTE. The corroboration requirement is met, and in any event that factor may never be used to deny a claim that is otherwise proven.

No traffic advisory exonerates this route. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses and carrying a validity window overlapping the trip. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00107-01, has a null payload — a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 that names no road and carries no window, so it exonerates nothing under POL-RD-03 and the driver's congestion excuse stands unsupported. Its absence is itself citable under POL-GEN-02, and it is the reason the driver's traffic point fails rather than a reason to excuse the excess.

Nothing in the chat log shifts the excess to the rider. POL-RD-04 exonerates only a detour attributable to a rider instruction, and the two-message log shows the opposite: the rider asking 'why exit at whitley? CTE goes straight down what' and the driver replying 'cte very jam tonight boss'. There is no rider request, and waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and no distance between leaving and rejoining the corridor is excluded.

Nor is the baseline moved by relocation or pooling. POL-RD-05 cannot run: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no amended optimal to re-apply the threshold against. POL-RD-12 cannot run: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so the matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The booked 14.0 km optimal therefore stands as the sole baseline.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, the fare_model being METERED and no exculpatory clause applying: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + 0.80 = (21.02 x 1.35) + 0.80 = 29.177, where the 1.35 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and not from the trip record, which carries no such field and would otherwise halve the figure. Refund = 36.60 charged_total less 29.177 = 7.423, rounded up to 7.45 payable. That is a 20.3% share of the charge — below the 90% full-refund line and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor — so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not NO_ACTION and not FULL_REFUND.

There is no pass-through line to settle separately. The fare breakdown shows an empty gantry list, tolls_erp of 0.00 and optimal_route_erp of 0, so no off-route ERP correction arises and nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure under POL-RD-09(1), which forbids double-counting ERP already comprehended in the recomputation. No phantom line exists to trigger a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4).

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, there are no gaps, max_gap_sec is 0 and the sampling interval is a steady 10 seconds, well inside the 30-second limiter. No limb (a) to (c) fires, so the deviation is established on the gps_trace itself and needs no independent corroboration — though the driver's own admission supplies it in any event.

None of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers fires, so the rider is entitled to a monetary ruling rather than a held file: the identifiers all match TRP-00107, the trace is clean, the refund of 7.45 does not exceed charged_total, and no charge line is unmatched. The driver's traffic point is an uncited assertion discarded under POL-RD-08, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so the POL-RD-10(5) limb is not engaged and the case should be decided, not escalated.

claims.text: The deviation on this trip is established but NOT material. On the governing GPS figure — trace_distance_km 17.57 km against an optimal of 14.0 km — the excess is 3.57 km / 25.5%, which clears the 20% / 0.8 km establishment gate in POL-RD-01 but sits far below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate. Because the deviation is non-material, no materiality-triggered consequence runs against this driver: no POL-RD-06 pattern treatment and no full refund. The rider's description of the detour as serious cannot lift the remedy above the partial refund the policy computes. POL-RD-01 also requires the trace figure to govern, so the slightly larger 17.6 km convenience copy on the trip record must not be used for the threshold test.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established against this driver, so the case cannot be escalated on reputation and no full-refund uplift is available. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 619 — a rate of about 0.0016, roughly a thirtieth of the 0.05 threshold — and the single flag is far below the alternative threshold of 3 flags. Under POL-RD-06 no pattern is ESTABLISHED. POL-GEN-01 confines those two fields to that one test, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is a near-synonym trap that may not be substituted for the 90-day figure.

Any refund must be recomputed with the surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown, where it is 1.35 and nowhere else. Under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + 0.80 = 29.177, so the exposure is charged_total 36.60 less 29.177 = 7.423, rounded up to SGD 7.45 — well under the $12.00 the rider contests. Treating surge as absent would roughly double the refund and is contrary to POL-RD-02.

The route change was a good-faith response to congestion on the CTE, as the driver told the rider in the chat at 21:26 ('cte very jam tonight boss') and repeats in his statement, and POL-RD-03 is the clause that would exonerate him. That clause cannot be run on this record: the only traffic advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00107-01, carries a null payload, so it lacks the named road, validity window and shortest-lawful-alternative figures POL-RD-03 requires. That artifact is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and its absence is itself citable; the impaired weight is disclosed rather than presented as clean. Because an exculpatory clause is invoked against an artifact that lacks the field the clause requires, POL-RD-10(5) directs ESCALATE — the disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer who can obtain the advisory, not refunded on a defence the record does not let anyone test.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this dispute cannot be decided on the record as it stands, so it goes to a human reviewer and the $12.00 in dispute is held — it is neither collected nor refunded. An escalation is terminal and replaces any money ruling.

What is established. The trip was longer than the route the platform computed at booking. The GPS trace measures 17.57 km against a 14.0 km optimal route — an excess of 3.57 km, or 25.5% of optimal. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern over the rounded 17.6 km convenience copy on the trip record. That clears the establishment gate (over 20% and over 0.8 km) but not the materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so the deviation is established and not material. The rider's profile shows 5 deviation claims in 60 days with 1 substantiated, so a claim below 30% needs corroboration beyond the trace; that is supplied by the driver's own statement that he went by Newton and Kim Seng. The trace itself is clean (100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) do not bite, and POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not move the baseline (no rider instruction, no amended endpoints, not a pooled trip).

The driver's defence and why it stops the ruling. The driver says the CTE was jammed near Chin Swee on Saturday night and he went by Newton and Kim Seng to avoid it. A traffic justification is a POL-RD-03 matter, and POL-RD-03 requires a traffic advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route uses and carries a validity window covering the trip. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00107-01, is an empty placeholder: its payload is null, it names no road and carries no window, and it stands at weight 0.0. An exculpatory clause (POL-RD-03) has therefore been invoked against a cited artifact that lacks the fields the clause requires, and POL-RD-10(5) makes escalation mandatory in exactly that situation. The rider is right that this advisory exonerates nothing; that is precisely why the record cannot test the driver's defence, and the answer is a human review rather than a ruling against the driver on a defence the record does not allow anyone to check.

What the figures would have been. Had a usable advisory been in the record, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic (METERED fare; surge 1.35 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is where the multiplier lives, not the trip record) would give recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 14.0 + 0.28 × 24.0) × 1.35) + 0.80 = 29.177, and a refund of charged_total 36.60 − 29.177 = 7.423, rounded up to $7.45 — not the $12.00 claimed. No repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06 (deviation_flags_90d of 1 against 619 completed trips; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only and was not used), so no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral arise. There is no ERP gantry and no surcharge line, so POL-RD-09 corrects nothing and POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity does not fire. No clause produces a referral here.

What would resolve this. The LTA traffic advisory for the CTE for 18 July 2026, roughly 21:00–22:00 SGT, showing whether a closure or congestion advisory was in force and, if so, the shortest lawful alternative distance. With that advisory the POL-RD-03 defence can be tested and the case decided — on the figures above if it fails, or on exoneration with the off-route ERP pass-through treatment in POL-RD-09(2) if it succeeds.

To the rider: your route-deviation complaint is partly upheld and you are refunded SGD 7.45.

The platform's own record establishes the deviation. The governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00107) measures the trip at 17.57 km; the booked optimal route was 14.0 km. The excess is 3.57 km, or 25.5% of optimal — above the 20% and 0.8 km establishment thresholds in POL-RD-01, so a deviation is established. It is below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality thresholds, so it is NOT a material deviation: no full refund and no driver-conduct referral follows.

The refund is arithmetic, under POL-RD-02, on the metered fare: recomputed fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 14.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.35 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = (21.02 x 1.35) + 0.80 = 29.177. The 1.35 surge multiplier is read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00107), the only artifact that carries that field — the trip record does not carry it at all. You were charged 36.60 (EV-FARE-00107). Refund = 36.60 - 29.177 = 7.423, rounded UP to SGD 7.45. That is 20.3% of the charge: above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund line, so the outcome is a partial refund of 7.45, not the 12.00 you contested.

Your claim needed corroboration beyond the trace because your profile shows 5 deviation claims in 60 days with only 1 substantiated and your excess is under 30% (POL-RD-08). It is corroborated: the driver's own statement admits he went via Newton and Kim Seng, i.e. the off-optimal corridor, which is one of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names.

To the driver: your explanation does not change the distance you are responsible for. POL-RD-03 can excuse a detour only where a traffic advisory names a road or segment the optimal route uses and covers the trip window. The only advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-00107-01) has no content at all (null payload, weight 0.0), so it exonerates nothing, and your account of congestion is a general assertion unsupported by any usable advisory — POL-RD-08 leaves it without weight. POL-RD-04 does not apply (the chat log shows the rider querying the exit, not requesting it, and no waypoint_hint); POL-RD-05 does not apply (no endpoint was amended); POL-RD-12 does not apply (the ride was RYDE_X, not a pool).

On your escalation argument (POL-RD-10(5)): the case is decided, not held. The advisory is present in the pool but empty, and you rely on no artifact the record actually lacks; a bare traffic assertion is governed by POL-RD-08, which fixes who loses when the fact is simply unknown, not by POL-RD-10(5). The rider's claim is proven on a clean, unimpaired GPS trace (100% coverage, no gaps, steady 10-second sampling, POL-RD-07 satisfied) and on arithmetic the fare breakdown supplies.

No ERP, toll or surcharge line exists (empty gantry list, 0.00), so no pass-through correction and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises. No driver compensation is due: the fare was billed at 17.6 km against a traced 17.57 km, so there is no unbilled distance. One open point for the file, not for the money: the LTA advisory returned empty for this trip — if a valid CTE advisory for that evening is later produced, your congestion defence could be revisited under POL-RD-03.
